name: slopster
title: Slopster
description: Reveal-shape openers and cross-sentence negation-correction, from the Slopster Vale styles. Its JargonSwaps list duplicates the slop-gate candidate set and was skipped; its em-dash rule is a count, not a match, and is discussed in the research log.

rules.name: Reveal-shape tell
rules.description: The "here's the hidden truth people get wrong" framing, which survives rewording because it is a shape rather than a phrase.
rules.suggest: State the thing directly instead of teasing it, and stop casting the reader as the one getting it wrong.

hit: What nobody tells you is that the migration takes a week.
This is what most people get wrong about caching.
miss: Nobody told us the deadline had moved.
Most people prefer the shorter route.

rules.name: "Not in the job description"
rules.description: The stock reveal that the real work is the unglamorous part.
rules.suggest: Say what the work actually was.

hit: Debugging the vendor's SDK was not in the job description.
miss: The job description listed three requirements.

rules.name: "The part people skip"
rules.description: Gesturing at a neglected detail rather than stating it. Close cousin of the shipped `thats-the-part`.

hit: Here is the part everyone skips.
miss: The parts department closed at five.

rules.name: Negation then correction, across a sentence break
rules.description: "X isn't A. It's B." — the correction split over two sentences, so a within-sentence rule misses it.
rules.suggest: Say what it is. The denial adds nothing the assertion does not.

hit: The bottleneck wasn't the database. It was the retry loop.
This isn't a rewrite. That's a rescue.
miss: It isn't clear yet whether the fix holds.

rules.name: "In an era of …"
rules.description: Scene-setting opener that delays the subject.
rules.suggest: Delete it and start with the subject.

hit: In an era of cheap compute, correctness is the constraint.
miss: The era of mainframes ended quietly.

rules.name: "Whether you're an X or a Y"
rules.description: The false-inclusive opener that addresses everyone and therefore no one.
rules.suggest: Address the reader you actually have.

hit: Whether you're a beginner or an expert, this guide helps.
miss: We will ship it whether you are ready or not.
Whether you are ready or not, it ships.

rules.name: "Think of X as …"
rules.description: The explanatory analogy reflex, reached for before the plain description.
rules.suggest: Describe the thing before reaching for a metaphor.

hit: Think of the cache as a shelf near the door.
